description: Order of the checks of an enrollment request in the Relay Specification v0 (draft), RELAY-v0.md section 5.1, as symbolic cases: no keys, no URLs, no signatures. A case has steps; each step is one POST of a gateway to the enrollment endpoint, made of symbolic parts, and the error the operator answers with (ok for a success). kid names who the request claims to be (self: the installation under test; unpaired: an installation that was unpaired; unknown: an installation URL that exists nowhere; none: a jwk instead of a kid), to the URL the request is sent to (self: the installation under test; other: a second installation of the same test account; unpaired, unknown: as for kid; or pair, key-change, certificate), header the url in the protected header (same as to, or different), nonce (fresh; used: a nonce an earlier request used up; unknown: one the operator never issued; previous: the nonce of the previous step of the case), signature (valid, or foreign: a good spelling signed with a key that belongs to no installation, with the algorithm of the claimed key), alg (key: the algorithm of the key, or other: the other algorithm) and payload (none: a read; csr: a certificate request; extra-member: an update with a member the schema does not list; not-object: a JSON array; duplicate-member: a member twice; noop: an update that changes nothing; unpair). world says what the operator has to hold before the case: both-active (two installations), other-unpaired (the second one unpaired), or, only offline, blocked, offline (the installation has been without a valid tunnel certificate for longer than max_offline_days) and offline-blocked. A live test cannot make an operator block its test account or wait for days, so the cases with offline set to true are played offline only, against the reference operator of this repository (RELAY-v0 section 8.3). Which defect each case finds is in why; the order is the list of RELAY-v0 section 5.1.

cases.why: a jwk on a URL other than pair is malformed (step 2)
a kid on pair is malformed (step 2)
a kid that names no installation is bad-signature (step 3)
one installation can never act on another: the kid of self at the URL of other is malformed
the URL of another installation is judged in step 3, before the signature of step 4
an alg that does not match the key of the installation is malformed (step 4)
a signature that does not verify is bad-signature
the signature is checked before the nonce: a bad signature with a used nonce is bad-signature (step 4)
a nonce the operator never issued is bad-nonce
a nonce is accepted once: a used nonce is bad-nonce
the nonce is checked before the url of the header (step 4)
a url in the header that is not the URL of the request is malformed, and the nonce is used up whatever happens next
a request object is closed: a member the schema does not list is malformed (step 6)
a payload that is no JSON object is malformed, before the signature is looked at (step 1)
a payload with a member twice is not I-JSON and malformed (step 1)
a regular read succeeds
the installation of an unpaired kid answers unpaired (step 3)
unpaired comes before the signature: the kid of an unpaired installation with a bad signature is unpaired
unpaired comes before the nonce: the kid of an unpaired installation with an unknown nonce is unpaired
unpaired comes before the URL: the kid of an unpaired installation at another URL is unpaired
the kid of an active installation at the URL of an unpaired one is malformed
a blocked installation can read and unpair
every other request of a blocked installation is blocked (step 5)
past max_offline_days every request but a read is offline-too-long (step 5)
offline-too-long takes precedence over blocked (step 5)
